Table of Unusual Observations in a Regression

Source: R/unusual.points.table.R
unusual.points.table.Rd

Identifies the observations of a fitted regression that should be investigated – high-leverage points, outliers, influential points and bad leverage points – and returns them in a table, as LaTeX (for PDF reports) or plain text (for the console), like the other snazzieR summary tables.

Usage

unusual.points.table(
  model,
  title = "Unusual Observations",
  latex = TRUE,
  id = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  leverage.cutoff = NULL,
  residual.cutoff = 2,
  cook.cutoff = NULL,
  flag = c("leverage", "outlier", "influential"),
  n.max = NULL,
  digits = 4
)

Arguments

model

A fitted lm or glm object.

title

Table title (its LaTeX caption). Defaults to "Unusual Observations".

latex

Logical; if TRUE (default) returns a LaTeX table. If FALSE, prints a plain-text table and returns the underlying data frame invisibly.

id

Optional labels to identify observations: either the name of a column in data (e.g. "Name") or a vector with one label per row of the data the model was fitted to.

data

The data frame the model was fitted to. Only needed when id is a column name and the data cannot be recovered from the model's call.

leverage.cutoff

Leverage threshold. Defaults to \(2(p+1)/n\).

residual.cutoff

Threshold for \(|\)standardized residual\(|\). Defaults to 2.

cook.cutoff

Cook's distance threshold. Defaults to \(4/(n-2)\).

flag

Which criteria make an observation unusual: any of "leverage", "outlier" and "influential" (default: all three). For example, flag = c("leverage", "outlier") leaves out points that are only flagged by Cook's distance.

n.max

Maximum number of observations to list (default NULL, no limit). When more are flagged, the n.max with the largest Cook's distance are kept and the legend says how many were left out.

digits

Number of significant digits shown. Defaults to 4.

Value

If latex = TRUE, a LaTeX table of class "snazzieR_table" (see snazzieR_table for interactive previews). If latex = FALSE, the table is printed and a data frame with one row per flagged observation (sorted by Cook's distance) is returned invisibly. Its "cutoffs" attribute holds the thresholds used.

Details

Diagnostics are computed with hatvalues, rstandard and cooks.distance, so the function works for any lm fit (including weighted fits, factors, transformed variables and missing values) and for glm fits (using deviance residuals). Observations with zero weight are excluded, as in plot.lm.

An observation is listed if it meets at least one of these criteria (defaults follow Sheather, A Modern Approach to Regression with R):

High leverage

\(h_{ii} > 2(p+1)/n\), twice the average leverage, where \(p+1\) is the number of estimated coefficients.

Outlier

\(|r_i| > 2\), where \(r_i\) is the standardized residual. (For large data sets a cutoff of 4 may be more appropriate.)

Influential

Cook's distance \(D_i > 4/(n-2)\).

Bad leverage

both high leverage and an outlier.

For each flagged point the table reports its observed and fitted response, leverage, standardized residual, Cook's distance and flags. A legend under the table explains the flags and compares the number of outliers with the number expected by chance.

See also

diagnostics.plots, model.summary.table

Examples

model <- lm(mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars)

# Plain-text table, labelling cars by name
unusual.points.table(model, latex = FALSE, id = rownames(mtcars))
#> == Unusual Observations ==
#> 
#> 
#> Obs                   Observed   Fitted   Leverage   Std. Resid.   Cook's D   Flags                      
#> --------------------  ---------  -------  ---------  ------------  ---------  ---------------------------
#> Chrysler Imperial     14.7       9.192    0.1865     2.355         0.4236     outlier, influential       
#> Maserati Bora         15         12.74    0.3942     1.12          0.272      high leverage, influential 
#> Toyota Corolla        33.9       28.05    0.0995     2.379         0.2084     outlier, influential       
#> Fiat 128              32.4       26.6     0.07991    2.332         0.1574     outlier, influential       
#> Lincoln Continental   10.4       9.363    0.209      0.4497        0.01781    high leverage              
#> Ford Pantera L        15.8       16.55    0.2044     -0.3227       0.00892    high leverage              
#> 
#> Flags: high leverage = h > 0.188 = 2(3)/32 = 2(p+1)/n;  outlier = |std. resid.| > 2;  influential = Cook's D > 0.133;  bad leverage = both.
#> Outliers: 3 of 32 observations have |std. resid.| > 2; about 1.5 would be expected by chance.

# Only the 3 most influential, ignoring points flagged by Cook's D alone
unusual.points.table(model, latex = FALSE, id = rownames(mtcars),
                     flag = c("leverage", "outlier"), n.max = 3)
#> == Unusual Observations ==
#> 
#> 
#> Obs                 Observed   Fitted   Leverage   Std. Resid.   Cook's D   Flags         
#> ------------------  ---------  -------  ---------  ------------  ---------  --------------
#> Chrysler Imperial   14.7       9.192    0.1865     2.355         0.4236     outlier       
#> Maserati Bora       15         12.74    0.3942     1.12          0.272      high leverage 
#> Toyota Corolla      33.9       28.05    0.0995     2.379         0.2084     outlier       
#> 
#> Flags: high leverage = h > 0.188 = 2(3)/32 = 2(p+1)/n;  outlier = |std. resid.| > 2;  bad leverage = both.
#> Outliers: 3 of 32 observations have |std. resid.| > 2; about 1.5 would be expected by chance.
#> Showing the 3 with the largest Cook's D of 6 flagged observations.

# LaTeX table for a PDF report
tbl <- unusual.points.table(model, title = "Cars to Investigate")
